svg.title: Echo headers on the response
svg.desc: Two checkout requests run one after the other. Request A sends X-Correlation-Id 7f3a, and checkout() returns a TicketResult. Before the 200 OK is written, a response filter reads X-Correlation-Id from the request and sets the same value on the response. Request B sends X-Correlation-Id c41e, and checkout() throws SeatAlreadyTaken. An exception mapper turns it into 409 Conflict, and the same response filter sets c41e on that response. Each caller gets back the id it sent.
svg.text: A response filter copies X-Correlation-Id onto the response, whether checkout() returned it or an exception mapper built it.

g.text: public void echo(ContainerRequestContext request, ContainerResponseContext response) {

svg.text: Request A calls POST /checkout with X-Correlation-Id 7f3a.
checkout() returns a TicketResult. Before Quarkus writes the 200 OK, the response filter runs.
The filter reads X-Correlation-Id from the request and sets it on the response, so the 200 OK leaves with 7f3a.
Request B calls POST /checkout with X-Correlation-Id c41e, for a seat someone else already holds.
checkout() throws SeatAlreadyTaken, so it never returns a response of its own.
The @ServerExceptionMapper turns SeatAlreadyTaken into a 409 Conflict response.
Response filters also run for handled exceptions, so the filter sets c41e on the 409.
Each caller gets its own id back. The same filter echoed it on the 200 and on the 409.
